AURORA

I was raised for one night.

One party. One red dress. One gun on my thigh, and one man at the end of it.

Adriano Castellani rules Florence. His family destroyed mine. I've spent my whole life learning how to get close enough to put a bullet in his heart.

I got close. I missed.

He should have killed me. That's the law in his world. Instead he carried me out of his own engagement party and locked me in his house on the hill.

Now he says I'll marry him or I'll die. He says one day I'll beg him for more than my life.

I'd rather burn.

But every night under his roof, I forget a little more which one of us is the monster.

ADRIANO

She walked into my engagement party in red silk and tried to kill me.

She was beautiful. She was fast. She was very nearly good enough.

By our law, she should be at the bottom of the Arno. My men are waiting for me to put her there.

Then I saw what was inked on her skin, and I knew exactly who she was.

So I kept her. I put my ring on her finger to keep her breathing.

She sharpens my grandmother's knives at my table. She bites when I kiss her. She swears she'll finish what she came to Florence to do.

Let her try. I'm not letting her go.

This is the first book in The Wildflower War Series. Reading order:

Wildflowers and Bullets.

Wildflowers and Blood.

Wildflowers and Bones.
